statement: Let n = len(target) and m = len(arr). Let L be the largest integer k with 0 <= k <= n for which there exist indices 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{k-1} < n and 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < m such that target[i_t] = arr[j_t] for every 0 <= t < k. Empty choices are allowed when k = 0. The function returns a result r and r = n - L; equivalently, r = len(target) - (length of a longest common subsequence of target and arr).
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values (for all i != j, target[i] != target[j]).

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail by panic, out-of-bounds access, or arithmetic overflow.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: The function returns a result r and 0 <= r <= len(target).
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= missing, where missing is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(target) such that target[i] != arr[j] for every j with 0 <= j < len(arr).
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: Let n = len(target). The function returns a result r and r = 0 if and only if target is a subsequence of arr, i.e., if and only if there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{n-1} < len(arr) with arr[j_t] = target[t] for every 0 <= t < n.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: Let n = len(target). The function returns a result r and r = n if and only if no value of target occurs in arr: for every i with 0 <= i < n and every j with 0 <= j < len(arr), target[i] != arr[j].
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0 if target[0] = arr[j] for some j with 0 <= j < len(arr), and r = 1 otherwise.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], target has no duplicate values, and len(target) = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and there exists an array a' of integers with len(a') = len(arr) + r such that arr is a subsequence of a' and target is a subsequence of a'.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every integer k with 0 <= k < r there is no array a' of integers with len(a') = len(arr) + k such that both arr is a subsequence of a' and target is a subsequence of a'.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: The function returns a result r and for every k >= 0 and every choice of indices 0 <= i_0 < ... < i_{k-1} < len(target) and 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{k-1} < len(arr) satisfying target[i_t] = arr[j_t] for all 0 <= t < k, one has r <= len(target) - k.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target) <= 100000, 1 <= len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.

statement: The function returns r1 on input (target, arr1) and r2 on input (target, arr2), and r2 <= r1.
preconditions: target, arr1, and arr2 satisfy the problem constraints: each array has length in [1, 100000] and all elements in [1, 1000000000], target has no duplicate values, and arr1 is a subsequence of arr2 (there exist 0 <= q_0 < ... < q_{len(arr1)-1} < len(arr2) with arr2[q_t] = arr1[t] for all 0 <= t < len(arr1)).

statement: The function returns r on input (target, arr) and r' on input (target, arr'), and r' = r.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints. Let v be an integer with 1 <= v <= 1000000000 such that v != target[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(target). Let arr' = arr ++ [v], and assume len(arr) < 100000 so that len(arr') <= 100000.

statement: The function returns r on input (target, arr) and r' on input (target', arr'), and r' = r.
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints. Let U be the set of all values appearing in target or arr. Let f be an injective function from U into [1, 1000000000]. Define target'[i] = f(target[i]) for 0 <= i < len(target) and arr'[j] = f(arr[j]) for 0 <= j < len(arr).

statement: Let P be the sequence obtained by scanning arr from left to right and appending i whenever arr[j] = target[i]; elements arr[j] not equal to any target value are skipped. Let I(P) be the length of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of P, with I(P) = 0 when P is empty. The function returns a result r and r = len(target) - I(P).
preconditions: target and arr satisfy the problem constraints: 1 <= len(target), len(arr) <= 100000, every target[i] and arr[j] lies in [1, 1000000000], and target has no duplicate values.
